PEG.one_line: NJ regulated electric/gas utility plus a long-life nuclear fleet (licenses extended to 2056-66) that data centers want for firm clean power.
PEG.reason: Guided 6-8% EPS growth (2026 guidance $4.28-4.40) plus real optionality from nuclear PPAs/uprates for PJM data-center load, yet trades at only 14.6x NTM with a 27% street upside after a pullback.

PPL.one_line: PA/KY regulated T&D utility riding a data-center-driven $23bn grid buildout with reaffirmed 6-8% EPS growth.
PPL.reason: Over 11 GW of signed data-center service agreements in PA and reaffirmed guidance support durable growth, while NTM P/E of 15.4x with negative FCF yield simply reflects growth capex, not distress.

SO.one_line: Southeast's largest regulated utility (Georgia Power, Alabama Power); Vogtle nuclear now complete and feeding Southeast data-center growth.
SO.reason: Top-tier scale, diversification and credit quality with the Vogtle overrun risk behind it; price is fair (17.1x NTM) rather than cheap, so this is a quality hold worth full diligence, not a bargain.
sources: general knowledge (Vogtle completion, Georgia data-center pipeline)

red_flags: PJM capacity price collar ($175-$325/MW-day through 2029/30) caps merchant upside; further FERC-mandated PJM governance reform due by end-Sept 2026 could add pricing constraints
VST.one_line: Merchant generator/retailer with nuclear and gas fleet, the highest-profile AI/data-center power trade in the sector.
VST.reason: Stock is down 30-36% from its 2026 high purely on fear that the PJM price collar caps future capacity revenue (auction has cleared at the $325 cap three straight years), even as EBITDA and guidance keep beating; at 13.7x NTM P/E with 57% street upside this looks like an overreaction worth full diligence, balanced against real regulatory-ceiling risk.

WEC.one_line: Wisconsin regulated utility with a growing large-load pipeline (Microsoft and other data centers building in-territory).
WEC.reason: Low volatility, consistent regulated growth, and an emerging data-center demand tailwind; price is fair rather than cheap but quality and growth both clear the bar.
sources: general knowledge (Mount Pleasant/SE Wisconsin data-center buildout)

ATO.one_line: Best-in-class credit-rated gas utility (Texas/Louisiana/Mid-States) doing steady pipeline-safety capex.
ATO.reason: Top-quintile margins (28.5%), lowest volatility in the batch and a rare A-grade balance sheet justify a full look even though growth is modest and the stock is not cheap.

red_flags: Pending going-private acquisition by a BlackRock-led consortium at $15.00/share cash; current price $14.87 is already ~99% of deal value, leaving negligible fundamental upside from here
AES.one_line: Independent power producer/renewables developer being taken private by BlackRock at $15.00/share.
AES.reason: This is a merger-arbitrage situation, not a fundamental research candidate; the cheap headline P/E and negative FCF yield are irrelevant once a fixed cash deal price is in place.

red_flags: Net debt/EBITDA ~7.2x is elevated for the sector and the 3x leverage target has been pushed out to 2029 to fund data-center buildout
NRG.one_line: Merchant generator scaling a multi-GW data-center power pipeline with GE Vernova/Kiewit and hyperscaler contracts.
NRG.reason: EBITDA +34% YoY, reaffirmed guidance and a new $3.2bn/1GW+ hyperscaler deal with capacity payments covering 95% of projected FCF, yet the stock has been sold off alongside VST on PJM price-cap fears to 9.5x NTM P/E; leverage is the real thing to underwrite in full diligence.

AEE.one_line: Missouri/Illinois regulated utility (Ameren) with a multi-year grid-modernization capex program and emerging load growth.
AEE.reason: Solid regulated quality and fair pricing; the data card's low single-year forward EPS growth figure looks like a comp-year artifact against Ameren's longer-run 6-8% guided growth rather than a real deceleration, worth confirming in diligence.

CMS.one_line: Michigan regulated utility (Consumers Energy) with one of the sector's most consistent multi-year 6-8% EPS growth records.
CMS.reason: Cheapest NTM P/E (15.4x) among the high-quality regulated names in this batch for above-average guided growth; leverage (6.3x) is typical for CMS's securitization-heavy structure, not a new concern.

red_flags: Elevated leverage (6.3x net debt/EBITDA) and $1.8bn of 2026 debt maturities including $1bn convertible notes to refinance
CNP.one_line: Houston T&D utility executing a regulator-approved $2.9bn storm-resiliency capex plan atop accelerating Houston load growth.
CNP.reason: 8% EPS growth guidance reaffirmed and the post-Beryl resiliency settlement removes a major overhang, but the near-term debt maturity wall and negative FCF yield (-21%) warrant a close balance-sheet check in full diligence.

red_flags: Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind (81% complete) cost estimate rose another ~$300m to $11.7bn; remaining construction/turbine-installation execution risk
D.one_line: Virginia electric utility at the center of 'Data Center Alley' demand, finishing the largest US offshore wind project.
D.reason: Contracted data-center capacity hit ~51 GW and guidance was reaffirmed, but subpar ROE (8.3%), heavy capex (FCF yield -17%) and a live offshore-wind cost/execution risk keep quality and price_vs_growth at 'fair' rather than clearly cheap after the stock's recent run.

red_flags: Highest leverage in the batch (net debt/EBITDA 7.7x)
DTE.one_line: Michigan regulated utility plus non-utility gas storage/pipeline assets, guiding to strong EPS growth.
DTE.reason: 32% forward EPS growth against a 14.8x NTM multiple is a large apparent gap even after allowing for a constructive Michigan regulatory backdrop; leverage is the item to underwrite before advancing conviction.

ED.one_line: NYC regulated utility (Con Edison); safe and well-run, but the slowest grower and most fully priced name in the batch.
ED.reason: Lowest forward EPS growth (6.6%) and lowest street upside (6.7%) in the group after a 10% momentum run, consistent with the prior v1 'excessive' valuation flag; good business, but priced for more than the growth on offer.

red_flags: Florida hurricane/wildfire physical risk flagged by the company as a monitored risk factor (not a California-style liability regime)
NEE.one_line: Largest US utility plus the leading renewables developer (NEER), with tax credits safe-harbored and supply chains locked in through 2027-29.
NEE.reason: Reaffirmed 8%+ EPS CAGR guidance through 2032 (and targeted through 2035) with hedged policy risk; the data card's negative single-year forward-EPS figure looks like a comp-year artifact, not a change in the multi-year growth story, but price is fair rather than cheap given the strong recent run.

NI.one_line: Indiana/Ohio gas-and-electric utility funding renewables/grid conversion capex, deliberately running a low payout to fund growth.
NI.reason: Low dividend yield (1.5%) reflects a growth-funding choice after the Blackstone electric-business minority stake sale, not distress; ~20% forward EPS growth at a fair multiple merits a full look.

red_flags: California's 2026 legislative session adjourned without wildfire-liability reform; Fitch moved PG&E's outlook to Negative (already one notch below investment grade); company launched a strategic review and cut 2027 capex by $2bn in response; BMO estimates a ~$10/share liability drag
PCG.one_line: California electric/gas utility still carrying unresolved, potentially unbounded wildfire liability exposure.
PCG.reason: The cheap headline P/E (7.0x) and huge street upside (56%) are a distress discount for genuine tail risk, not a value signal — this is close to the disqualifying 'leverage stress / major litigation-regulation' pattern the triage is meant to catch, so it is passed rather than advanced despite the model rank.

red_flags: Elevated leverage (net debt/EBITDA 7.7x, tied for highest in batch)
PNW.one_line: Arizona Public Service parent, benefiting from Phoenix-area population and data-center growth but running above-average leverage.
PNW.reason: Solid but unexceptional on every dimension (quality 3, growth 3) at a fair price — a reasonable hold, not a standout that clears the bar for a full diligence slot this round.

SRE.one_line: California/Texas utility (SDG&E, Oncor stake) plus Port Arthur LNG export, de-risking via a $10bn infrastructure-stake sale to KKR/CPPIB.
SRE.reason: The sale of 45% of Sempra Infrastructure and third-party equity funding (Blackstone/KKR/Apollo/Goldman) for Port Arthur Phase 2 materially reduce Sempra's own capital burden and balance-sheet risk going forward, so the eye-catching -54% FCF yield mostly reflects legacy megaproject capex rather than the forward run-rate; 14.4x NTM P/E for 63% guided EPS growth looks cheap.

red_flags: Residual Colorado wildfire (Marshall Fire-related) liability overhang, largely settled/insured but worth a light check
XEL.one_line: Minnesota/Colorado regulated utility with a growing hyperscaler data-center pipeline and the highest street upside in the batch.
XEL.reason: 24% forward EPS growth at 15.8x NTM P/E with 31% street upside is an attractive combination for a regulated utility; the Colorado wildfire liability item is largely resolved but merits a quick confirmation.
sources: general knowledge (MN/CO data-center pipeline, Marshall Fire settlements)

AWK.one_line: Largest US investor-owned water utility; best moat in the batch (no fuel/commodity exposure) but the most expensive.
AWK.reason: Highest NTM P/E in the group (20.3x) with the lowest street upside (8%) and only mid-single-digit growth beyond guidance — top quality, but priced for more than it is currently delivering, so it is a hold rather than a full-diligence pick this round.
